text: For second-timers, some face difficulties paying the resale levy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For those with difficulties, we are prepared to look at them and consider incorporating the levy into the purchase price.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many of them who are second-timers are also looking to get the flat urgently.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, for them, the better option is really to consider the resale market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: PHG can help in this respect because that grant is available to second-timers, too.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, even if you are a second-timer, you buy from the market, first of all, there is no resale levy to pay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For those in rental, we have put in place a new Fresh Start scheme to support them in their home ownership journey.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For the elderly, I touched on this in last year's COS, we have many schemes to help them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have built 2-room flexi flats for them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, they are priced with a significant subsidy to make sure that they are affordable.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For first-timers, they, too, are eligible for grants, which will make the 2-room flexi flat very affordable for them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have also made other enhancements last year, including deferring the downpayment until key collection for the elderly, when they right-size, providing a temporary loan, one-to-one counselling and an elderly priority queue at the HDB Hub.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All these measures have helped, and we will continue to see what more we can do to support our elderly.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For the singles, that is another group that many Members talked about – Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Alex Yam.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So far, more than 12,000 singles have bought new 2-room flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The application rates are still high, I recognise that and we are doing our best to build more 2-room flats to clear the backlog.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the last five years, 27,000 have bought resale flats, more than the ones who have bought new flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, the enhancements to PHG will make this a more attractive option.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I hope this will provide more options to singles in the resale market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about the minimum age of 35 for singles to buy HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: He mentioned that Singaporeans are marrying later, but the marriage rates are still high among singles under the age of 35.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I think the age of 35 is still valid today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In any case, as I have mentioned earlier, we still have a backlog to clear, and we should focus on that and make sure that for those who are in the queue, we will build enough 2-room flats to help them get their 2-room flats first.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Another group that many Members talked about are divorcees.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members asked whether we can help them make a smoother housing transition, especially for the benefit of their children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, we recognise that divorce can be a stressful and emotional period, and a complex process with many decisions to be made.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB provides advice to families on their post-divorce housing options to make their housing transition smoother.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We help them purchase a BTO flat through the Assistance Scheme for Second-Timers (ASSIST), where they get priority when applying for a 2- or 3-room BTO flat in the non-mature estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the interim, before their flat is ready, they can rent a subsidised flat from HDB under PPHS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB also offers rental housing to those in need, including those who need help to tide over a protracted or acrimonious divorce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One issue that divorcees may face is the time bar for purchase of subsidised flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think Mr Louis Ng mentioned this just now.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a rule put in place in 1997 whereby, during the time bar, a divorced couple can only own one subsidised flat between them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, both sides have to agree on who should be allowed to buy the subsidised flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is what we call the "mutual consent" agreement or requirement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The time bar was set at five years initially, and we have reduced it to three years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We hope that this will help divorced persons provide a more conducive living environment for their children and go some way to help families through an already difficult period of transition.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to do our best to help these and other groups, including single unwed parents with children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We already exercise considerable flexibility for such appeals, as I have elaborated upon in previous sessions, and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We look at each case carefully and consider what is in the best interest of the child and, if necessary, we will assist the parents, or the parent and child, in purchasing a flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon will elaborate on how else MND is helping families in transition and various vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides upholding home ownership, we must continuously look at ways to improve the way we build our future Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Poorly designed cities can easily become a high-rise concrete jungle.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We get all the problems associated with rapid urbanisation – crowding and social fragmentation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The city becomes a stressful and alienating place to live and work in.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But, at their best, modern cities with well-designed buildings and neighbourhoods can connect people and improve our well-being.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we must innovate and explore new ways of building to achieve even better results.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One important shift is to push for higher quality and higher productivity in construction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is especially crucial, given the major pipeline of projects that are coming up in the decade.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have embarked on many programmes and we have rolled out an ITM.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second Minister Desmond Lee will share about this in his speech later.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For my part, I would like to touch on two important areas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, how can we build a more inclusive Singapore?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Earlier in the Budget Debate, several Members talked about the importance of addressing inequality, bridging social divides and enhancing social integration.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think everyone here recognises that it is a complex issue that involves multiple strategies on the economic and social fronts.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our urban and living environment also has a part to play to bring residents of diverse backgrounds together, promote social integration, and uplift the lower-income.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, how can our built environment help to foster a more inclusive Singapore?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have a few suggestions and these are areas that we are working on.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: BCA publishes guidebooks and develops standards for Universal Design and disseminates them to the industry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, our efforts have received recognition from outside parties, like the United Nations (UN), which praised Singapore for our "user-friendly built environment".

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: BCA is looking at raising the bar further as part of our review of the Accessibility Master Plan and Accessibility Code.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will be engaging stakeholders, including public users, in this process.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will pay special attention to the elderly, given our rapidly ageing population.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All HDB estates are now barrier-free and we will see how we can further improve.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Darryl David asked about the Government’s plans for the EASE programme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are studying what more we can do under EASE.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members also asked if we can enhance the designs of our flats to support our elderly.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have been looking at this and have introduced better designs for elderly-friendly estates and flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Within this area, HDB flats for seniors are integrated with a continuum of social and health services, so that the residents have easy access to all the services "under one roof".

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The feedback from the residents who have moved into Kampung Admiralty is very positive and we will study how this can be implemented in other areas as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond better integration, we will go further by exploring assisted living.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Assisted living is a model of living that integrates home and care.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, within one block or even on the same floor, you can have individual apartment units together with shared communal facilities for dining, social activities and a range of eldercare services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will pilot this in HDB flats and we will also study ways in which this can be done in private developments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is our first point on making the future Singapore more inclusive, in the way we design our buildings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The second area is to ensure that our housing estates continue to have common spaces, public parks and greenery for all to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is critical, especially in our compact high-rise living environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew started this with the push to make Singapore a Garden City.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When we spoke with him in 2012 and asked him what more should we do to take Singapore forward, this is what he said: "Singapore must retain the sense of space.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We're going to build taller buildings but we can’t build them closely together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There must be a sense of playing fields and recreational areas for children and old people – a sense that this is a full country with all the facilities which you expect of a large country but in a confined space." This is the challenge that our planners have and they are very conscious of this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is reflected in the way we design our HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They do not always have a large green field site to work with.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some sites come with constraints and they have to work around these constraints.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They may not get everything perfectly right but we take in feedback, as many have shared, and we will continue to improve our designs for new estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For existing estates, we also have programmes to rejuvenate our estates, existing ones, to keep them vibrant and liveable.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We recently unveiled plans for Toa Payoh, Woodlands and Pasir Ris for public consultation, and we will finalise the plans later this year and start works thereafter.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is part of our efforts to provide support for the construction industry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we are bringing forward projects, particularly to help the industry during this period.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the flat level, we have HIP, which several Members highlighted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members have asked about expanding the scope of HIP and extending it to flats built after the existing cohort.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I have shared in this House previously, any upgrading programme is a major commitment that spans many years and would cost billions of dollars.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We had just had a major debate on the Budget about fiscal sustainability and how Government spending is rising sharply, and how we need to raise revenues to meet these future needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Any future upgrading programme has to be studied very carefully in this context.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Eventually, when the proposals are put forward, I hope Members will support more resources for MND to do upgrading in existing estates as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is our second area where we want to make sure that our estates have common spaces, parks, greenery that all can access and enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Thirdly, we can also facilitate more social interactions within the block itself.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We already have the Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) to ensure a better racial mix.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also try to mix different unit types within the same block, something which several Members spoke about.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, in the past, we would build standalone blocks of studio apartments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Now, all 2-room flexi flats launched are integrated with other flat types within the same block.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For rental flats, likewise, these are the same considerations when we build rental flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We try not to cluster too many rental flats together, and try to build them together with sold flats in the same neighbourhood so that residents can share and access the same communal facilities and amenities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The flats are still under construction but we will learn from this experience, get feedback about the lived experience in these flats and, if it is positive, we will certainly want to do more.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Importantly, it is also about how you design the block to maximise opportunities for social interaction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some of these things, I would acknowledge, happen more through serendipity than deliberate design.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I give an example of how, in the past, we did not have lifts on every floor.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the lift landing somehow became a place where neighbours get to meet one another.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I say this from personal experience because my HDB apartment was on the 21st floor on a lift landing, just next to the lift.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the neighbours come and we get to meet them all the time, and you can have a chance to talk to them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, lift landings are on every floor, so you do not have as many opportunities for interaction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think it is a good thing, but you do not have that many opportunities to meet.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have to use other design methods to encourage neighbourly interaction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why in some of the new BTO flats, for example, in Dawson, HDB has tried out more seating areas in the common spaces near lift lobbies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are trying out more greenery and rooftop spaces for residents to get together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are different designs that are being piloted, that we are trying out.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, it is something that we have to learn by doing, and from the experiences and feedback that we get, we can improve for each new project that we embark on.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, one major thrust in how we want to build our future Singapore is to make sure that we are more inclusive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Another major emphasis in the way we build for the future is to make sure we have a more Distinctive Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We cannot just be another modern city, one amongst many in the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have to be a city that stands out – stand out not by having the biggest, tallest or fanciest building but through our distinctive character and culture, our heritage and identity.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means capitalising on our strengths – our city in a garden, our clean and safe environment and our multicultural diversity and heritage.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Part of our shared memories is captured in our buildings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we are, indeed, paying more attention to heritage elements in our planning process, as highlighted by Mr Alex Yam.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Buildings with historical significance will be preserved or conserved and repurposed for other uses, as we have done with some of the buildings like the former Supreme Court and City Hall.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some old buildings may have to go but, even in doing so, we can find ways to preserve the memories of the place.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is the approach we took for Dakota Crescent.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have heard the many calls for the place to be kept.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There was a ground-up initiative by several architects to do this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Such efforts demonstrate that it is possible for us to combine both old and new to bring out what is distinctively Singaporean, and this is what we will do also for the Rail Corridor.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is a unique space where we can celebrate our heritage, culture and biodiversity, and it will connect close to one million Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we are reviewing our plans around the Corridor, as Ms Low Yen Ling has suggested, to see how we can best make use of this unique space.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I agree with Ms Low’s suggestion that it is important that the Rail Corridor is accessible to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have been working closely on this project with the community, anchored by the Friends of the Rail Corridor comprising residents, students and nature and heritage groups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As enhancement works for this central four-km stretch commence later this year, we will also improve accessibility to the Rail Corridor from adjacent developments like homes, schools, workplaces and transport nodes, including having new access paths in the nearby Hillview neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In parallel, we will implement trail improvement works along other stretches of the Rail Corridor this year, so that virtually the entire stretch of the Rail Corridor will be connected seamlessly.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Rail Corridor will also serve as a gateway to parks and trails island-wide.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will intersect with the upcoming Coast-to-Coast Trail, which will span across Singapore from Jurong Lake Gardens in the West to Coney Island in the Northeast.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, even as we embark on our next phase of development, we are committed to enhancing our City in a Garden and making Singapore an even greener and more beautiful home for all to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have shared our plans for our future city and home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To achieve these bold plans, we need to work together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are building up capabilities, not just within the Government but also, as Mr Alex Yam said, amongst our architects, engineers, consultants and builders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I agree with Mr Darryl David that the Government needs to partner the community, interest groups, businesses and industries in building our future city.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are many opportunities to co-create the common spaces in our HDB towns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All of us see this in our estates but this one was different.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They worked together on the project from conceptualisation to design, to even the final assembly of the playground onsite.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It took longer than usual – about two years to build this playground.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is much longer than the normal time it would take to build a playground.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Residents shared that they love the project, they take pride in it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because they take ownership of the playground, they were involved in it, they appreciate and enjoy it much more.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a meaningful way to shape our common spaces together and we hope to do more of this in other estates, too.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to enable such ground-up initiatives to shape our neighbours.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB already provides support for residents to activate their community spaces and we hope that more would take up the funding support from HDB.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One example is a project titled "Welcome to our Backyard" led by residents and volunteers in Aljunied Crescent.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, Members can see the before and after pictures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: What was before was an empty grass patch and, because of the community involvement, they took ownership of it, they transformed it into a warm welcoming backyard with swings and mini gardens.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides our neighbourhoods, we have also supported many community-initiated projects in our public spaces all over Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, a group of stakeholders in Kampong Glam had an idea to spruce up a small park at Sultan Gate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With URA’s support, they installed park benches, picnic tables, lighting and even a giant swing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Now, there is a cosy spot for the public to gather and interact.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are just two examples of the wonderful things that can happen when everybody takes ownership of the places we live and work in and we shape our urban landscape together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is tremendous potential for all of us to do more together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As a nation of home owners, all of us have a part to play in shaping our future city and home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the last 50 years, we have transformed from mudflats to a metropolis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Let us now work together on our next lap of urban transformation to be a green, smart and liveable city, and to be a vibrant global city that is inclusive and that is distinctively Singaporean, a place we are all proud to call home.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank Members Mr Ong Teng Koon and Mr Baey Yam Keng for their interest in MSO's work.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Most of them are straightforward and dealt with quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A good number require multiple agencies to work together to resolve them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These issues could range from the provision and maintenance of local infrastructure, such as footpaths and railings across different land boundaries, to complex problems, such as hoarding of items in HDB flats.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MSO was formed three years ago to improve coordination for these cross-cutting issues.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The various initiatives undertaken by MSO to improve coordination, such as appointing lead agencies to settle municipal issues regardless of land ownership, have borne fruit.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These initiatives have resulted in the public’s needs being addressed more effectively and more promptly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They are adopting a more collaborative and resident-centric approach in handling interagency issues.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There is a shift in mindsets in serving the public.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: One such example was how NParks and HDB worked together on a request for a staircase connecting Clementi Avenue 6 and Ulu Pandan Park Connector.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It seemed like a simple request, but there were complications.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The area was earmarked for future public housing development and, hence, the staircase had to be planned with future developments in mind.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NParks dealt with the presence of high-tension cables underground by using lightweight precast slabs to minimise deep excavation works.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A ramp was also thoughtfully added at the side of the staircase for cyclists to access the Park Connector.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There are many of such examples, which illustrate how our agencies are working well together and addressing residents’ needs holistically.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While we see more of such efforts, there remain municipal issues falling in grey areas where MSO can play a role to help.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As Mr Ong Teng Koon had rightly pointed out, MSO focuses heavily on improving interagency processes which are not apparent to the public.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Town Councils oversee the cleaning of common areas, AVA takes enforcement action against pigeon feeders, while NEA takes enforcement action in instances where high-rise littering is involved.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Residents' Committees (RCs) of the People's Association (PA) are often roped in to counsel the feeders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These agencies work together in order for pigeon-related issues to be resolved holistically.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To support their efforts, MSO has helped to formulate end-to-end workflows to clarify roles and responsibilities and tighten coordination in their handling of such pigeon-related nuisance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Similar processes have also been developed by MSO for other complex issues, including animal hoarding, involving AVA, HDB, NEA, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and social welfare agencies; and the management of outdoor display areas, involving Town Councils and the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Moving forward, MSO will continue to engage our residents and stakeholders to identify more of such grey areas where we can improve coordination and support the agencies and Town Councils in their efforts to serve residents better.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As we improve processes, we also need to ensure that our platforms and solutions continue to meet residents’ evolving needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Ong had asked about the take-up of the OneService (OS) platforms to date and plans to use the platform to better reach out to our residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is the result of MSO constantly improving the OS platforms to better serve the needs of our residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Back then, it had six reporting categories and allowed residents to report municipal issues to Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, the Facilities in HDB Estates and Shared Bicycles categories introduced last year allow members of the public to report municipal issues in HDB estates to the Town Councils, and indiscriminately parked Shared Bicycles to bike operators.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This makes it more convenient for residents to report on issues they encounter and also enable Government agencies and Town Councils to collect data more systematically to guide future planning and operations through studying trends and analysing hotspots.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MSO has also introduced the OS Portal, which aggregates municipal information for residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This includes information from diverse sources which are of interest to residents, such as block washing schedules, e-waste recycling points and HDB's Welcome Parties.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our goal is to transform the OS channels into a one-stop community platform that can meet residents' diverse municipal needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In the coming year, besides providing feedback and accessing information, residents will also be able to use the OS channels to perform transactions, participate in community events and give their feedback and comments on local improvement programmes to help co-create their living environment.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In the long term, we hope to make the OS channels a one-stop platform to address their municipal needs comprehensively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through the use of digital technology, MSO aims to bring about greater convenience to our residents and also to make it easier for residents to engage with Government agencies and Town Councils and actively participate in shaping their living environment.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As MSO works with our partners to improve the effectiveness of our solutions and platforms, we also work with Government agencies to improve productivity and cost efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is especially important in the manpower-lean environment today.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked if there is scope for greater integration in the area of cleaning between the work of Government agencies and Town Councils in order to achieve greater efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: That is a good suggestion, which MSO will study.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: However, MSO wants to move even more upstream, by improving processes at the planning and design stage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Good planning and design make our municipal infrastructure cheaper to upkeep in the long run.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The guidelines on the design of new public infrastructure will make them easier to clean and support mechanisation efforts by cleaning contractors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Beyond cleaning, MSO is also looking at how to improve processes to facilitate timely and efficient responses to local infrastructure requests.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While there are well-established funding schemes, such as LTA’s Walk2Ride Scheme, and MND's Estate Upgrading Programme (EUP), funding gaps for small-scale infrastructure at the local level do exist from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These are small-scale but nevertheless important requests that make a positive difference to residents’ daily living, such as having handrails up a footbridge crossing Geylang River, and lightings along a footpath near Punggol Point Light Rail Transit (LRT) station.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Besides LIP, MSO has also worked with our partner agencies to develop escalation mechanisms so that conflicting demands or constraints among the agencies do not result in undue delays in the planning, development and maintenance of connectivity-related infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will help to bridge the gap and support our agencies in meeting local infrastructure needs of residents more responsively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To conclude, municipal service delivery has made significant progress.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Leveraging the combined efforts of Government agencies, Town Councils and residents, MSO has worked to reduce overlaps and duplications, plug gaps in the municipal landscape and deliver better living experiences for our residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MSO will continue to facilitate collaboration, build capabilities and harness technology, so as to enable the delivery of cost-effective and quality municipal services for residents and a better living environment for all.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Chairman, at the appropriate juncture, may I show some slides?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Saktiandi asked how we will create a high-tech built environment sector that creates good jobs for Singaporeans and improves opportunities for local firms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the past year, the Government has been partnering our industry, unions and institutes of higher learning (IHLs) to formulate ITMs for key sectors in the Built Environment cluster.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are construction, real estate, security, environmental services and landscaping.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These five sectors cover the span of the infrastructure lifecycle, from conception, design and construction to operations and maintenance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to help firms level up their capabilities, seize new opportunities and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we are now shifting gears to implement these plans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, the Construction ITM focuses on two areas to improve productivity and competitiveness in our sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA) and Integrated Digital Delivery (IDD).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: DfMA involves the prefabrication of building components in a highly automated and mechanised manner, just like the manufacturing process, before onsite assembly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This saves time, reduces our reliance on low-skilled foreign labour, and results in more consistent quality.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As Minister Lawrence Wong had said, we need to make major shifts in the way we build to achieve better results.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Driving DfMA adoption for greater productivity is one such decisive shift.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And to help our firms do so, we will continue to create lead demand and, at the same time, build more Integrated Construction and Prefabrication Hubs (ICPHs) to ensure a sufficient supply of prefabricated building components.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also pushing for greater adoption of Building Information Modelling (BIM) and Integrated Digital Delivery (IDD).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As Mr Saktiandi has described, BIM helps firms visualise detailed building designs in virtual 3D form before they are actually built, thus minimising potential issues during construction.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: IDD builds on top of BIM to connect various project parties through digital information.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It also provides useful information about the building, for future maintenance or retrofitting.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also drive IDD adoption so that our built environment sector can reap further benefits from the entire construction and building lifecycle.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To facilitate this, we will develop shared platforms and standards to increase IDD interoperability across the entire environment value chain.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Many smaller firms are also building up their capabilities in DfMA and IDD.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One such example is a local firm called Tong Hai Yang, which is a homegrown construction and interior firm.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The firm set up a subdivision to explore DfMA and this led it to develop its modular Prefabricated Bathroom Units (PBUs) as well as customised solutions to improve the fabrication and onsite deployment of its product.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Another example is Shin Construction, a local small and medium enterprise (SME) specialising in plumbing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As a plumbing subcontractor for residential developments, Shin’s adoption of BIM helped eliminate potential clashes between mechanical, electrical and plumbing pipes and air-conditioning ducts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This helped the project team avoid abortive works and delays during the construction phase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As Er Dr Lee Bee Wah noted, local contractors also need to build up their capabilities and track record to succeed both locally and abroad.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In this regard, Er Dr Lee said that stringent prequalifications in Government projects could prevent local firms qualifying and, hence, building up relevant experience.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We should clarify that prequalifications are not intended to limit opportunities, but to ensure that tenderers have the ability to tackle important and complex public works, such as MRT or deep tunnelling projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While it is up to agencies to set their own requirements, they certainly have to be fair and not be unduly onerous.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They should also ensure that their tenders obtain an adequate number of bids, to ensure fair competition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our approach to help firms is to give them the resources they need to build up their capabilities, so that they become more competitive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, contractors can tap on various schemes under BCA’s Construction Productivity and Capability Fund (CPCF) to build up their capabilities and to upgrade their workforce.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In tandem, we also reviewed our procurement framework to place more emphasis on quality and this will facilitate healthier and more sustainable competition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With improved capabilities, local contractors will better their chances of qualifying for more construction projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition, we will also try to help our local firms internationalise, if they wish to do so, by finding opportunities for them to team up for large overseas ventures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If our firms can offer together a unique "Singaporean" way of undertaking the entire development cycle, such as through BIM and IDD, this will certainly enhance their competitive edge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One example of an opportunity is in Amaravati, the new capital city of the state of Andhra Pradesh in India.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Singapore companies with the relevant expertise should consider whether they can export their services there as part of the consortium.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the property transactions space, we aim to streamline the process to make it more convenient for buyers, sellers and agents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For FM, our goal is to transform the way we maintain our infrastructure so that we can be more efficient and effective.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan is quite right when he said that we need to make good use of technology and better streamline our building management operations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is especially important as our buildings and infrastructure age and as we continue to face manpower constraints.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will, therefore, encourage building owners and MCSTs to invest in better and more effective FM solutions, such as real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will streamline their processes, enhance user experience and reap long-term cost savings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This, of course, will depend also on demand that the buyers of these services, such as condominiums, industrial properties and commercial buildings recognising the value and the savings that can be reaped through having smart FM capabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also encourage consultants and developers to systematically consider maintainability outcomes in the design and construction phase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will enhance the sustainability of our buildings by reducing lifecycle maintenance costs arising from inefficient design.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are many synergies among the various ITMs under the built environment Cluster.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Platforms developed under one ITM could also benefit companies in different stages of the building lifecycle.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Firms in this ecosystem can do much more to work together across functions and sectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While its initial focus will be to implement the Construction ITM, its longer-term goal is to reap synergies from the various ITMs in the built environment cluster.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Build.SG will work closely with Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs), IHLs and unions to engage our industry and turn our ITM plans into action.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In particular, it will focus on helping firms build capabilities and deploy key technologies and deploy key technologies and lending support to firms keen on exploring overseas opportunities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Build.SG will also act as a one-stop career office to attract, retrain and upskill professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) in the built environment domain.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Those working in the sector must also upgrade themselves to continue to thrive in the industry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And employers need to provide their employees with opportunities to do so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: After graduating from the Institute of Technical Education (ITE), Shaban joined JTC in 1995 as a lift technician carrying out lift maintenance work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With JTC’s encouragement, he expanded into more complex areas, such as Building Management Systems.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Eventually, his expertise enabled him to start taking on greater responsibilities, including supervising less experienced technical staff.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: He is now a key member of JTC’s Building Management Division, overseeing day-to-day operations in the J-Ops Command Centre, which is a centralised command nerve centre that monitors building operations and performance across JTC’s buildings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There, he works with building managers and engineers in building diagnosis and fault detection.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have invited Shaban to contribute to the improvement of the FM sector at the national level through FMIC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And I am glad that he has agreed to take up this challenge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is people like Shaban, with real, deep skills and experience who thrive on new challenges, continuously upgrade their skills and who are passionate about their work that will enable us to transform our built environment sector and provide new opportunities for Singapore firms and Singaporean employees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We hope that the industry and research community will collaborate with us in this journey to transform the built environment sector through innovation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So far, we have spoken about our efforts to transform the built environment sector to grow our economy and create good jobs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, as our city ages, and as our focus also begins to be on FM and maintenance of the city, we will also need to find ways to future-proof our infrastructure, so that it continues to be safe and functional.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong has asked how we ensure that buildings are designed and constructed to be structurally safe, enforce regular maintenance and checks, and grow a sustainable pool of local skilled technical staff to support this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are already measures to ensure building safety.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, developers must appoint a Qualified Person (QP), who is a registered PE, to carry out structural design.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for more complex works, the design must be checked by independent Accredited Checkers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A QP and site supervisors must supervise building works to ensure that they are done in accordance with the approved plans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Building materials must also comply with prescribed standards and be tested by accredited laboratories.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: BCA will conduct site audits to ensure compliance with requirements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: BCA also requires regular inspections to ensure buildings remain structurally safe.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: BCA will continue to engage stakeholders on implementation details to minimise the burden of cost.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also support the new façade inspection regime by introducing inspection guidelines and strengthening R&D efforts to look into more effective and productive ways to carry out façade inspections.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This could include the use of camera-equipped drones to check building façade conditions which, I understand, has been used overseas, by companies like Industrial Skyworks in Canada and Wiss, Janney, Elstner Associates in the US.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I also agree with Mr Chong Kee Hiong that proper lift maintenance is important and that is why we earlier tightened BCA's maintenance regime for lifts to ensure their safety and functionality.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For HDB lifts, in particular, we have also put in place additional procurement and maintenance processes to improve lift safety and performance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are continuing to improve these processes and are now studying how to better evaluate downstream maintenance costs in the procurement stage, so that HDB can better differentiate between lift suppliers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, we are studying the evaluation of tender pricing over a longer time period via longer lock-in maintenance period for lift suppliers, as well as placing higher weightage on quality score, as compared to price score, in tenders.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The other part of the equation is to build a sufficient pool of competent personnel to conduct the required checks and servicing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Last year, BCA and our Labour Movement formed the Lift and Escalator Sectoral Tripartite Committee (STC) to look into ways to professionalise the industry and to attract more locals to join the sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I understand that STC will provide its full recommendations later this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But one recommendation being seriously considered is a voluntary progressive wage model (PWM) for local lift technicians.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Each wage level will be defined by specific skillsets and responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This sets out clear progression pathways for lift technicians and ensures they are remunerated appropriately for their skills and effort.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We hope that companies will come on board and work together to build up a sustainable pipeline of skilled local lift technicians.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is also important for us to ensure that our public housing remains safe and well-maintained.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In that regard, some Members have asked if we can do more to address maintenance issues faced by flat owners.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Generally, while we strive to minimise downstream maintenance through high-quality construction, flat owners also play a part in maintaining the flats as they age.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nonetheless, HDB has, on a goodwill basis, continued to assist flat owners should they raise maintenance issues, and advise them on possible follow-up actions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition, we offer heavily subsidised upgrading works under HIP to address common maintenance issues for older flats built up to 1986.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For issues, such as ceiling leaks and spalling concrete, which occur outside HIP, residents can apply for a 50% subsidy under HDB’s Goodwill Repair Assistance (GRA) scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is more generous than the private sector provision.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Taken together, these measures, including efforts at the local level, have helped keep the maintenance cost of our flats low for the majority of HDB residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Now, let me briefly address the remaining cuts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah spoke about difficulties faced by some landed property owners in accessing their neighbours' property to undertake repairs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If home owners face such difficulties, they can seek help from their Neighbourhood Committees or other dispute resolution channels, such as the Community Mediation Centres, to try to resolve the issues amicably.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, we will study to see if legislative changes are needed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Sylvia Lim spoke about owners of landed properties affected by breakaway works.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are already requirements on the homeowner to ensure that any breakaway works are done properly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes plastering and painting the exposed wall.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The appointed QP has a professional duty to ensure that the works are structurally safe and done in accordance with all requirements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Should issues like water seepage arise later on, we encourage owners and neighbours to resolve them in an amicable manner, or via dispute resolution channels, which I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Png Eng Huat asked about the allotment of Heavy Vehicle Parking (HVP) spaces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: His concern is about the availability of HVP at the local level.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I understand that in his discussions with URA, as part of the ongoing master plan discussions, he has raised these queries, and we will continue to address them at the local level.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: URA also allows mutual exchanges of season parking locations amongst drivers within its HVPs through an online platform.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Through such measures, we hope to assist Heavy Vehicle drivers with their parking issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Likewise, we continue to encourage employers to play their part in providing the necessary commute facilities for their staff.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong asked if designs could be improved to mitigate noise pollution from vehicles in multi-storey car parks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Specific to car parks, HDB considers the orientation and distance between them and residential blocks, and the placement of physical barriers, such as communal facilities as well as greenery, to screen the noise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to incorporate good planning considerations and make use of technology where appropriate, such as noise modelling, to mitigate noise impact.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong also asked about the impact of prefabricated construction methods on home owners' renovation options.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under both traditional and prefabricated construction, home owners are not allowed to hack or remove structural elements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, flats built with prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC) tend to have thicker structural columns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, we no longer provide kitchen walls, so that home owners need not hack them during renovations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Since 2015, HDB has also used drywalls for non-load-bearing internal partition walls and these are easier to remove, compared to traditional concrete walls.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Lastly, some Members have spoken about animal issues and human-animal interactions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang described his most recent experience working with AVA on animal protection issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked for stricter laws against animal feeding, particularly for cats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In this regard, AVA has been working with AWGs and other agencies to educate the public about responsible feeding practices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We believe that this combination of measures in both education and enforcement will help to reduce irresponsible feeding over time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In this process, we will continue to future-proof our existing infrastructure to ensure that they remain safe and functional for the long term.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Collectively, we will continue to shape our urban environment into one that affords new and exciting opportunities for Singaporeans in a vibrant and exciting future city.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, let me begin by thanking Mr Darryl David and Mr Leon Perera for their comments on our local agricultural sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: FTM provides a platform that brings together Government agencies, industry players and IHLs to transform our farming sector to become more resilient and productive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: FTM remains a "live document" that is constantly updated based on evolving needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am glad to report that we have made progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is the first time that AVA is tendering out land using the Fixed Price tender method.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This allows tenderers to compete on concept as opposed to price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Proposals will be evaluated based on production capability, track record, relevant experience, innovation and sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Any farmer who is committed to being productive and has a good track record will stand a good chance of winning the tender.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It started out growing vegetables using traditional farming methods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But in 2012, the owner Mr Chan Yow Tiong, decided that the farm needed a new approach in order to stay competitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, he brought in Mr Desmond Khoo, a technologically savvy 25-year-old entrepreneur with strong marketing skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Khoo also owned a few vegetable stalls in wet markets, as well as a fresh food import business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through this complementary partnership, the farm began exploring innovative ways and technologies to increase their productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This shows that with the right partners and mindset, farmers can, indeed, take their businesses to the next level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, this ongoing series of tenders will provide existing farmers with a clean slate of sorts to bring in new technology and transform the way they operate, without the encumbrances of previously existing operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There are also opportunities for farming in unconventional spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Rooftops are interesting possibilities in our highly urbanised environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In 2014, we piloted Singapore's first rooftop farm, Comcrop, at SCAPE mall in Orchard Road.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We saw its potential to scale up and facilitated conversations between Comcrop and JTC for a 35,000 square feet rooftop space on one of JTC's food factories in Woodlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With space the size of seven basketball courts, Comcrop has now finalised plans to develop eight high-tech greenhouses with environmental controls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to push for such innovative projects to optimise our land use and to grow our urban farming movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But farm transformation can only succeed if the industry takes the lead to embrace innovation as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, in this regard, I am glad that a few members of AVA's Industry Consultation Panel came together last October to form the Singapore Agro-Food Enterprises Federation (SAFEF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SAFEF aims to represent, advance and promote the agro-food sector in Singapore for economic development and for export.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a ground-up initiative, SAFEF's founding members collectively contribute more than 50% of our locally grown produce and represent some of our most productive food farms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Having these progressive farmers band together to walk this journey with us makes me confident that we can raise the sector's productivity and improve our food security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I look forward to more farmers joining SAFEF and working closely with us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Indeed, we want to do even more together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have worked closely with the industry and taken on board their feedback to review existing schemes and develop new initiatives to better support our farmers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, we will further enhance the Agriculture Productivity Fund (APF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many farmers have told us that they are happy to adopt more productive technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, new farming systems require heavy capital investments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Advanced greenhouse systems with environmental controls and automation, which can double their production, can cost around S$4 million.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond the capital cost of implementation, farmers have told us that they need assistance in testing these new systems prior to a larger-scale deployment, to ensure that the technology can be adapted to our local conditions and produce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It will provide a talent pipeline to ensure our farms have skilled manpower to undertake transformation and innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For a start, Temasek Polytechnic will launch its new "Earn and Learn" work-study programme to attract ITE graduates into the aquaculture industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am glad that six of our food fish farms have already pledged support for this programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The graduates will start their 12-month attachment programmes from April this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I hope that our farmers will, indeed, take this opportunity to create a positive learning experience for the graduates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will help encourage our young talent not just to enter the industry, but also to stay and contribute more to the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Third, we will do more to help increase demand for local produce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As our farmers become more productive, they will naturally need more consumers to support them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In this context, we organised the first SG Farmers' Market last September at myVillage mall in Serangoon Gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: More recently, we co-organised the second Farmers' Market last month with SAFEF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: More than 25 local farmers participated and I am happy to say that most of them sold out all their products to the crowds that visited the Market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Five busloads of my own Yio Chu Kang residents visited the Market and snapped up the produce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I have heard good feedback from my residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I also know that many of our grassroots organisations organised groups to support the event.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I urge consumers, especially Singaporeans, to support our fresh and nutritious local produce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These efforts will strengthen the ecosystem and operating environment for our farms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But as the industry matures, we also need to start looking at the wider food value chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to work towards creating an enabling environment to keep our local agricultural sector commercially viable and sustainable for the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Everyone wants a safe haven to call home, but some may have lost their homes or have been displaced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Several Members have highlighted that this can be a difficult time for these families, and asked for assistance for single parents, families in hardship and our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some may have no family to turn to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They also cannot buy an HDB flat until the divorce is finalised and their housing eligibility and budget are clear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will deal with them on a more flexible case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan spoke about the housing needs of widowed Non-Residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Now, following the demise of their Singaporean spouse, they may retain the flat with a Singaporean family member.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Where there are young children involved, HDB can allow the flat to be retained in trust for the children or let those with no other housing options rent a flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap asked for our housing policy to better cater to unmarried parents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We encourage those who can live with their family to do so, for mutual support with childcare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But each family has different needs and circumstances and, therefore, we will exercise flexibility where needed, to ensure that every child has the opportunity to grow up in a stable and secure environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As Mr Saktiandi Supaat highlighted, families in financial hardship may end up without a place to stay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And they may worry about being rejected from public rental because of past property ownership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, HDB takes a needs-based approach in assessing applications for public rental.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: HDB considers their income, whether family members can accommodate them, and the applicant’s ability to afford a flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This takes into account also the sales proceeds from their previous property, if any.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have updated the eligibility criteria for public rental to make these considerations much clearer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Several Members asked about how we help Singaporeans who do not meet the public rental eligibility criteria and how we cater to larger families with children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While the public rental income ceiling is one consideration, the cost of home ownership is another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Over the years, home ownership has stayed affordable, with more grant options and also higher grant quanta.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We want to encourage home ownership whenever possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Those who can afford to buy a flat, especially first-timers with grants, are not allowed to enter into public rental, even if their income is within the ceiling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On the other hand, others above the income ceiling may be accorded flexibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, larger families have higher expenses, which we account for when assessing their housing options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, a family of three can already rent a 2-room flat if they earn an income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: More than 90% of rental households have four or fewer registered occupants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For the larger families, most live in the larger flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is the result of HDB ramping up supply over the last decade to about 60,000 rental flats today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to monitor the need to build more rental flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some wait time, however, is inevitable as HDB assesses each application and considers the household's preferred location.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For those in urgent need, HDB may offer them priority allocation or interim rental.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For both rental and home ownership blocks, HDB and the Town Councils work together to ensure the cleanliness and maintenance of common spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested measures to help low-income seniors buy a flat, which we will study further.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, seniors already have the option of short-lease 2-room flexi flats, which are highly affordable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Dennis Tan's suggestions to reduce the singles premium are already in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is just over half of what they would pay for the same flat on a 99-year lease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also thank Miss Cheryl Chan for her suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) actively encourages Singaporeans to make an LPA and to do so early, this is ultimately a personal decision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also note her points on means-testing for seniors living in short-lease private properties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will study these issues further with the relevant agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Home ownership is a cornerstone of our nation and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how we are helping rental tenants with this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Thirty-one of them have booked a flat, of whom two will be collecting their keys this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: One of our Fresh Start families is the Chng family, who booked a flat in Yishun last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After collecting their keys, the family of four can receive up to $15,000 in grants over the next five years, which will grow their CPF savings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This means that eligible families may even be emplaced in the Fresh Start programme before the first rental tenancy renewal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Fresh Start is still a very new scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to consider further enhancements with the Advisory Committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We encourage all rental families, including those who wish to purchase a larger flat, to discuss their home ownership aspirations with HDB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On average, about 800 households move from rental into home ownership each year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Most of them are first-timers, helped by affordable flat prices and our generous housing grants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Rental families also get priority allocation under the Tenants’ Priority Scheme (TPS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After we expanded TPS to include second-timer families in 2016, 150 more families have benefited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After entering rental, Mr Ng found steady employment and grew his income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The family of five has recently moved into their own 3-room flat in Punggol.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I hope these data and examples will assure Members that we take a needs-based approach in providing assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue studying how to support families on their home ownership journey, and I look forward to sharing more of our progress next year.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Ministers for their replies to our cuts.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: A number of Members have raised this point but pardon me if I missed the response amidst all the answers.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The first is with regard to rental and this is directed to the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Many of our rental precincts tend to be a little bit sparse in terms of facilities and design.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: A number of Members spoke about the impact the living environment has on families as well as their children.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Is there more that the Ministry can do to provide better facilities for some of these existing precincts because the newer ones are seeing better facilities?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The second has to do with our older, single Singaporeans living in rental flats.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I think three Members raised this point that co-living together can sometimes bring about a lot of stress because of a lack of privacy.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Is the Ministry studying ways to provide a greater measure of privacy, especially for some of the older flats?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As a design, they are actually integrated with the other types of HDB flats of various sizes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As part of our Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) that is at the precinct level, the area will be enhanced.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This includes rental flats in the area as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And in the newer ones, I think beyond 2013 to 2014, for example, the partitions also include separate doors and a separate window so that there is a lot more privacy for these tenants co-sharing a unit.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Hopefully, it will reduce any chances of friction and to give them a lot more privacy.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This query is to do with the spalling concrete issues, particularly post-HIP and whether HDB can consider taking on a larger share of the GRA.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We addressed this in answer to a recent Parliamentary Question (PQ) as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
