text: If it is, indeed, poor-quality work by the GRA contractor, then we will ask them to rectify.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The first two are addressed to Minister Lawrence Wong.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Is there a delay and, if there is, why is there a delay?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The next two questions are addressed to Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For infrastructure projects that I mentioned where, when it comes to prequalification, the local contractors do not qualify.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: It is because they specify that they must have completed projects of certain size, very big size, so none of the local contractors qualify.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister, in situations like that, can BCA consider breaking down the project to smaller parcels so that the local contractors can have a share in it and to build up the track record.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Otherwise, they can never have a track record and go overseas.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The second question is about the feeding of stray cats.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Why is it that NEA said they cannot take action until it is left there for two hours or more?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Why do we waste time and resources to monitor those two hours?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The moment they walk away, it should be littering.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Can the Ministry work with NEA to sort this out?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Whether we can do more, it is something we would have to study.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, it would be based on various considerations, including availability of funding.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On HIP, our commitment was to complete selection by the end of the year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is consistent across various Ministers' speeches, I am sure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have kept to that commitment; we will finish the selection by then.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have given an estimate on when these projects will be fully implemented because the implementation varies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Sometimes, you need more time for consultation and so on.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It may be 2021, it may be 2022.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But that is really an implementation process rather than selection.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Desmond Lee, would you like to respond?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For certain complex projects, you will find that our local contractors also partner foreign firms which have that technical expertise and, in that respect, a certain degree of tech transfer and learning comes about.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, we have impressed upon our agencies that in setting these requirements, they have to be mindful that these are, indeed, necessary for the project and do not unfairly prejudice our local firms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I believe that the Member would have done well to raise it at MEWR's COS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Working with the community and animal welfare groups, we have been able, in certain areas, to have a mix between enforcement and educating the feeders to ensure that the area is properly upkept.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: What are they doing on water quality issues?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Thirdly, on the land tendering system, the Senior Minister of State talked about the changes to the system.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Would the Ministry give some consideration to whether the tendering system, whether it is a fixed price tender or a more traditional tender, does that disadvantage startups and SMEs versus a large agri-business or corporation?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: We may have an interest to ensure that at least some of the land goes to startups or entrepreneurs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Because whether it is on track record or financial resources, large agri-business corporations may have an advantage.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, I just wanted to know the Senior Minister of State's thoughts on that going forward.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Chairman, the first question on how much of APF has been disbursed, unfortunately, I do not have the numbers on hand right now.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But many of the farmers whom we had spoken to, as I said in my speech earlier, were keen to tap on the fund for technology to enhance their operations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some of them may have held back because of the ongoing land tender.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They wanted to wait for the certainty of lease.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That is why the 20-year lease that we put out for these new plots of land are extremely helpful for them to see how they can best amortise their investments over a longer timeframe.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On the Member's second question on the aquaculture, fishery sector and what AVA and the Government are doing to help them mitigate the risk of plankton blooms, we know that there were a couple of serious plankton blooms that happened in the recent past.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: AVA has also put up some R&D grants a few years back and encouraged fish farmers to use some of these grants to testbed solutions that will help them develop systems that protect their fish stocks from harm.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: About three to five local fish farms have used the funds quite well to adopt and create new technologies, like the closed containment systems, for which they can rapidly deploy and protect their fish stock when a plankton bloom does occur.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Having said that, they are still a very small portion of all the fish farms out there in the coastal areas.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And I think no one would be able to prevent a plankton bloom because these are exogenous factors relating to weather, relating to water conditions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: What it means is that more of our fish farms ought to tap on the grants to develop systems that mitigate some of these risks that are quite unpredictable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We want to encourage more of our fish farmers to use this and to do so, but they have to make the move.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We can provide the grants, we can provide the conditions, the expertise as well, but they must do so.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The third thing is on the fixed price tender.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is the first time we are doing the fixed price tender method.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: What it does is that we are no longer looking at bidding as a main determinant of who gets the plot of land.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: What it means is that it will not disadvantage smaller players compared to a big player which has got deeper pockets.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is the intent of why we go on to a fixed price model for this particular tender exercise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But first, let me say a big "thank you" to my now favourite Minister – Minister Lawrence Wong.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can I confirm that the removal of the mutual consent requirement is with immediate effect?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, does it apply to people who were divorced before the announcement today?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And third, can I check with Minister Desmond Lee whether we can increase AVA's budget?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The implementation details will be put up by HDB.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The timelines and who will be eligible will be all made clear.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I do not want to dwell on that now in terms of the time bar.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we do want to do it soon and we want to make sure that as many people will benefit from this lifting of the time bar as possible.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The third question is on AVA's resources, whether more will be given to AVA.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We manage with the allocated resources that MND has.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: AVA is given a budget like all of the agencies under MND.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We spoke earlier in the Ministry of Finance's (MOF's) COS, that every Ministry is striving to do more with less.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Just because I am the Second Minister for Finance does not mean that I get special pass.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All Ministries are trying to manage with more limited resources and the same applies to us and to our agencies within MND's purview.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Within the resources that we have, we encourage all agencies to do more.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If there is a need, a new function or new value that is created, new projects that they deem are worthy, then there is a central pool within our Ministry which we can re-allocate from, so that these meritorious projects are funded.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is what we will continue to do.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: One, what is the status of the uncompleted units left behind by LUP, that is, those that cannot be completed, that means, those that cannot be done in the past, there are still some?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: The second question is: what help can be given to those who are having financial difficulty who are renting a flat outside while waiting for their BTO flat?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: They cannot afford to pay the market rate.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Hopefully, they can get it slightly cheaper through the HDB's Interim Housing scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Chairman, on LUP, we gave an update not so long ago in a PQ.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I do not have the information with me now but we gave an update on those that have already been implemented.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have already said if there is anyone living in these sorts of blocks who need help, particularly with medical needs or mobility needs, then we can look at this and see how best to assist them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the second question, for those who have applied for a BTO flat and need rental, there is PPHS to help them.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think we have time for two more clarifications.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Chairman, with regard to the MPH design that I mentioned, will HDB be coming in to change the existing MPH design, the one at Hougang View Court and Hougang Meadow, where it is quite impossible to hold a decent funeral wake, especially on the last day, due to the passageway and due to the configuration of the MPH?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, again, it is a very local specific issue in this new BTO estate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am not familiar with it, but I will ask HDB to look at that particular issue and see whether there is any way to address Mr Png's concerns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I have mentioned earlier, in the HDB team, there is an inhouse architecture design team, but they also work with private architects.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They are continuously seeing how we can improve our designs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They may not always get it perfect because each time they do something in a particular new estate, there are site constraints and they have to work within all these constraints to put in place the BTO units as well as the amenities and facilities, sometimes in a quite constrained manner, especially if the site is not big enough.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, for this particular area, let me ask HDB to check and see if there is anything that can be done to address Mr Png's concerns.

text: I will allow the last question from Mr Yee Chia Hsing.

speaker: The Chairman
text: He has been putting up his hand for a very long time already.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: On this issue of helping local companies win Government contracts when they do not have the track record, can the Ministry also look at the experience at the individual level?

text: Mr Alex Yam, would you like to withdraw the amendment?
